sources.text:
10 wk summer placement, Brightwater Analytics (small fintech), Manchester, Jun-Aug 2026
team: me + 2 platform engineers (Mateo, Jen)
- goal: move the nightly risk batch jobs off one big VM onto EKS so they stop blocking each other
- stack: Terraform, EKS, Karpenter, Argo Workflows, Prometheus, Loki
- decision: spot instances for the batch node pool, on-demand for the Argo controller. cheaper, jobs are retryable anyway
- problem: jobs randomly lost progress overnight, ~5% of runs. cause: spot interruptions + checkpoints only every 10 min
- investigated via node termination events in CloudWatch + the job logs. the 2 min warning wasn't enough
- fix: checkpoint every 90 s + a drain handler on the termination notice
- result: nightly run 4h10m -> 2h35m, nothing blocked since
- learned: read the spot termination docs first, not after
- why Graphcore: liked the scheduling side more than the models. want to work on the platform under the models
I wrote the Terraform modules for the node pools and the Karpenter autoscaler config myself, and Mateo reviewed them.

documents.text:
During a ten-week summer placement at Brightwater Analytics in Manchester, our three-person platform team moved the nightly risk batch jobs from a single virtual machine onto EKS.

The stack was Terraform, EKS, Karpenter, Argo Workflows, Prometheus and Loki.

Jobs randomly lost progress overnight in about 5% of runs. The cause was spot interruptions combined with checkpoints only every 10 minutes. Investigation used node termination events in CloudWatch and the job logs. The fix was checkpointing every 90 seconds and adding a drain handler on the termination notice. I learned to read the spot termination documentation first, not after.

I wrote the Terraform modules for the node pools and reviewed Mateo's Karpenter autoscaler configuration. Mateo reviewed them.

Dear Graphcore hiring team,

I am applying for the Graduate Cloud Platform Engineer 2027 role at Graphcore.

I want to work on the platform under the models because I liked the scheduling side more than the models.

The 10 week summer placement at Brightwater Analytics, a small fintech, in Manchester ran from June to August 2026. The team was me and two platform engineers, Mateo and Jen. We worked to move the nightly risk batch jobs off one big VM onto EKS so they stopped blocking each other. We used Terraform, EKS, Karpenter, Argo Workflows, Prometheus and Loki. We used spot instances for the batch node pool and on-demand for the Argo controller. I wrote the Terraform modules for the node pools and reviewed Mateo's Karpenter autoscaler configuration. Mateo reviewed them.

The jobs randomly lost progress overnight in about five percent of runs. This was investigated through node termination events in CloudWatch and the job logs. The cause was spot interruptions and checkpoints only every ten minutes. We applied a fix to checkpoint every ninety seconds and add a drain handler on the termination notice. We reduced the nightly run from 4h10m to 2h35m with nothing blocked since. I learned to read the spot termination documentation first, not after.

Thank you for considering my application.

Kind regards, Ellie
